attempts.user_message:
Please review the following manuscript written by my collaborator.

Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

Here is the manuscript:

/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b06/review-experiment-a31isyjf/call-0c65f570cd6c4594b91f9fc4e14984d9/manuscript.pdf

command_activity.command: /bin/bash -c 'ls -la . manuscript.pdf && command -v pdftotext && command -v pdftoppm && command -v pdfinfo'

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
import importlib.util, shutil
for name in ['pdfplumber','pypdf','fitz','pypdfium2','PIL']:
    spec = importlib.util.find_spec(name)
    print(name, spec.origin if spec else None)
for name in ['gs','pdftotext','pdftoppm','mutool']:
    print(name, shutil.which(name))
PY"

/bin/bash -c "mkdir -p tmp/pdfs && python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
p = PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('PAGES', len(p.pages))
print('METADATA', p.metadata)
parts=[]
for i,page in enumerate(p.pages,1):
    parts.append(f'\\n\\n===== PAGE {i} =====\\n\\n'+page.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout'))
Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text(''.join(parts))
print(''.join(parts[:3]))
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
for path in Path('tmp/pdfs').iterdir():
    if path.is_file() and (path.suffix == '.png' or path.name == 'manuscript.txt'):
        path.unlink()
Path('tmp/pdfs').rmdir()
Path('tmp').rmdir()
PY"

strengths: Addresses an important practical setting: unlearning using only the pretrained model and forgetting data, without retained examples, surrogate data, or stored training trajectories.

Provides substantial experimental coverage across six datasets, three deletion settings, and 15 baselines, with additional ViT and VGG experiments. Reporting five-trial means and standard deviations, hardware, and baseline search ranges is useful.

Full-class and several subclass results are promising. MU-Mis achieves an average accuracy gap of 0.07 on CIFAR-100 and offers substantial runtime savings in some settings, such as 83 seconds versus SalUn’s 2630 seconds on Tiny ImageNet.

Sequential deletion experiments examine whether previously forgotten classes recover, alongside utility and output KL divergence. The component ablation in Table A6 provides concrete evidence that combining the target-class and other-class terms improves over either term alone.
weaknesses: The central theoretical connection is not established. Section III-B drops the dependence of intermediate training parameters on the training sample and derivatives of the softmax probabilities without bounding the resulting error. ReLU activation does not justify neglecting the sum of cross-sample contributions in Eq. (5), particularly for correlated samples. The cross-entropy derivative also has the wrong sign: it should be p−e_c. More fundamentally, sensitivity to perturbing a training input is not equivalent to the counterfactual effect of deleting that sample.

The proposed objective lacks a sufficiently supported connection to removal of training influence. Adding the same input-dependent function h(x) to every logit preserves all softmax probabilities but changes the difference of squared gradient norms in Eq. (8). Thus, the loss can change without changing predictive behavior. The before/after-training sensitivity histograms do not resolve this issue or directly validate the surrogate against leave-one-out influence.

The privacy evaluation does not support claims of robust protection or a privacy guarantee. The reported MIA metric is only the fraction of forgotten examples classified as members; without false-positive rates, an attack that always predicts nonmembership would score perfectly. Attack features, training splits, and calibration are insufficiently specified. Stronger attacks reporting ROC-AUC or detection at fixed false-positive rates, calibrated against retrained models, are needed. Dataset-averaged output KL also cannot establish indistinguishability and may conceal discrepancies concentrated on forgotten samples.

The strongest claims do not extend to random-subset deletion. In Table A5, MU-Mis has average gaps of 2.80 and 2.36 on CIFAR-10 and SVHN, versus 0.51 and 0.54 for fine-tuning. On CIFAR-10, forgetting accuracy remains 97.43% versus the retrained model’s 94.51%, while test accuracy falls to 91.50% versus 94.75%. These results show both incomplete matching of forgotten-sample behavior and material utility loss, limiting the broad claims of superior sample-level unlearning.

The claimed simplicity and robustness of stopping and tuning are insufficiently demonstrated. Figure 9 studies thresholds from 0.7 to 1.0 on one task, whereas Table A7 uses values up to 3.0 and sequential experiments use 10. Appendix C additionally introduces selective loss reweighting with κ=80, which materially changes the main-text algorithm but receives no dedicated ablation. Selecting the best utility separately for each sequential request does not demonstrate how suitable settings can be chosen without retained-data or retrained-model feedback.

Reproducibility and attribution of improvements remain incomplete despite the useful implementation details. The manuscript provides baseline repositories but no MU-Mis implementation link, and Table A7 omits settings for the random-subset experiments. The closest prior method, JiT, already uses input-sensitivity regularization; controlled comparisons with consistent batch-normalization handling, together with broader ablations of stopping and reweighting, would better establish which new components produce the gains.
